newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. troops to complete Kuwait deployment Monday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops to complete Kuwait deployment Monday.

text.p: The United States will complete by Monday the deployment in Kuwait of some 3,000 soldiers sent to defend the Gulf oil state against a possible Iraqi attack.

U.S. army Captain Tim Raymond told Reuters some 400 of the soldiers arrived in Kuwait earlier on Sunday, raising the total of U.S. troops already in the country to 2,500. Some 1,200 U.S. troops were in Kuwait before the latest Gulf crisis began.
The remaining 500 U.S. soldiers are expected to arrive in the Gulf Arab state in the next few hours. All 3,000 will be deployed by Monday night, Raymond added.
The deployment from Texas started on Wednesday.
The last of the 3,000 1st Cavalry troops flew out of the Fort Hood army base on Saturday on a 20-hour flight to Kuwait.

Arriving soldiers are taken immediately to Camp Doha, north of Kuwait City, where they spend about six hours drawing pre-positioned U.S. weapons, including main battle tanks, then head into the desert close to the border with Iraq.
Hundreds of them fired artillery and tank cannons in the Kuwaiti desert on Sunday in wargames aimed at deterring trouble from former occupier Iraq.
The troops carried out the live-fire exercise at the Kuwaiti military's Adera Range desert training area 40 km (25 miles) south of Iraq, Lieutenant Colonel Thomas Nickerson said.
They were training in unusually unpleasant, dusty conditions in the desert on Sunday. The sky over Kuwait City was darkened by a thick cloud of sand and dust stirred by an overnight desert storm.
The deployment is part of Washington's major buildup in the region which followed its September 3 and 4 cruise missile attacks against targets in southern Iraq.
The strikes were in retaliation for intervention by Iraqi forces in Kurdish factional fighting in northern Iraq.
